name: Strawberry
tagline: Sun-ripened, hand-picked and impossible to resist.
description: Picked at dawn and on a stall by eight. Our growers pick strawberries fully red and never chill them overnight, which is why they taste like actual strawberries.
origin: River Valley farms, 12 miles from the city
tips: Store unwashed in a single layer, covered loosely.
Bring to room temperature before eating — cold kills the aroma.
Hull them just before serving, never before.

name: Avocado
description: Grown on sheltered hillside groves and picked to order. Ours ripen on the tree longer than supermarket fruit, which is where the flavour comes from.
tips: Ripen in a paper bag with a banana; refrigerate once soft.
Leave the stone in the unused half to slow browning.
Choose fruit that yields gently at the neck, not the base.

name: Tomato
tagline: Heritage varieties grown for flavour, not freight.
description: Thirty-one varieties across our markets, from green zebra to oxheart. Grown in soil, picked ripe, sold within twenty-four hours.
tips: Never refrigerate — below 12°C the aroma compounds die.
Store stem-side down on the counter.
Salt ten minutes before serving to draw out sweetness.

name: Carrot
tagline: Sweet, crisp and pulled the same morning.
description: Sandy-loam carrots with the tops still on. Until you have eaten a carrot pulled that morning you have not really eaten a carrot.
tips: Twist the tops off on day one — they drain the root.
Store in a damp cloth in the crisper drawer.
Roast whole with the skins on for the sweetest result.

name: Blueberry
tagline: Small, deep and dusted with natural bloom.
description: High-bush berries from the lakeside beds, hand-rolled into punnets. That pale powder on the skin is the bloom — it means fresh.
tips: Do not wash until the moment you eat them.
Freeze in a single layer on a tray, then bag.
A squeeze of lemon makes them taste brighter.

name: Peach
tagline: Tree-ripened, freestone, and worth the sticky chin.
description: Orchard Lane picks peaches at the point where they leave the branch with a twist, not a tug. Everything else follows from that.
tips: Ripen in a closed bag, then refrigerate only if needed.
Skin slips easily once blanched for 30 seconds.
Grill cut-side down with honey and thyme.

name: Broccoli
tagline: Tight heads, sweet stems, cut cold.
description: Cut in the cool of the early morning and iced within the hour. The stalk is the sweetest part — never throw it away.
tips: Store stem-down in a glass of water like flowers.
Roast at high heat — boiling gives you nothing.
Peel and slice the stalk for slaws and stir-fries.

name: Spinach
tagline: Leaf, not baby leaf. Cut this morning.
description: Proper bunched spinach with a stem and an opinion. Washed twice, spun once, on the table within six hours of cutting.
tips: Wilt in a dry pan before dressing to avoid a watery plate.
Store rolled in a dry towel inside a bag.
Freeze blanched portions for winter cooking.

name: Pumpkin
description: Not the carving kind. These are dense, dry-fleshed varieties bred for the plate: Crown Prince, Kabocha, Rouge Vif.
tips: Cure in a warm room for a week before cooking.
Roast in big wedges, skin on, then scoop.
The seeds toast beautifully with salt and oil.

name: Apple
tagline: Heritage orchards, sixty varieties, no wax.
description: Unwaxed heritage apples from orchards that pre-date the motorway. Ask for a taste — most growers will cut you a wedge.
tips: Store cold, away from other produce — apples emit ethylene.
Pair by texture: sharp Cox, sweet Gala, aromatic Egremont Russet.
Cook with two varieties for depth.

name: Basil
tagline: Cut to order, sold by the armful.
description: Genovese, purple and Thai basil, cut to order so the leaves never bruise. Sold standing in water, which is how herbs should travel.
tips: Treat like flowers: trim stems, stand in water, out of the fridge.
Tear, do not chop — blades bruise the leaves.
Blanch and freeze in oil for winter.

name: Wildflower Honey
tagline: Raw, unfiltered, and from hives you can visit.
description: Unpasteurised honey from hives within nine miles of the market square. It will crystallise — that is the proof it has not been heated.
tips: Never microwave — stand the jar in warm water instead.
Crystallised honey is fine; it is not spoilt.
Buy by taste: spring honey is floral, autumn is dark and malty.

name: Sourdough
tagline: Thirty-six hour ferment, baked before six.
description: Stone-milled regional wheat, wild yeast, a thirty-six hour cold ferment and a bake that starts at four in the morning.
tips: Store cut-side down on a board, never in plastic.
Refresh a day-old loaf in a hot oven for six minutes.
Freeze sliced — toast straight from frozen.

name: Farm Cheese
tagline: Raw milk, single herd, aged on the farm.
description: Made within twenty miles of the stall by four small dairies. Raw-milk clothbound cheddar, soft ripened rounds and fresh curd.
tips: Take cheese out of the fridge an hour before serving.
Wrap in wax paper, not cling film.
Ask the maker what the herd was grazing on.

name: Free-Range Eggs
tagline: Deep yolks from hens that see daylight.
description: Pasture-raised, collected by hand and graded on the farm. The yolk colour is a direct readout of what the hens have been eating.
tips: Store pointed-end down, in the box, not the door.
An egg that floats is old; one that sinks is fresh.
Room temperature eggs whip to greater volume.

name: Citrus
tagline: Thin-skinned, heavy for its size, ridiculously juicy.
description: Lemons, blood oranges and satsumas from the southern growers who send one van north each week in winter.
tips: Choose fruit that feels heavy for its size.
Roll before juicing to double the yield.
Zest before you cut — always.
